sources.text:
Project: CI pipeline and preview environments for a student startup's web app (Bristol, part-time, Jan to Jun 2026). The team had five developers and no automated builds; every deploy was done from one laptop.

Goal: every pull request gets a preview environment with its own URL, and merges to main deploy automatically.

Technologies: GitHub Actions, Docker, a small Hetzner server running k3s, Traefik for routing, cert-manager for TLS, and a Postgres database per preview created from a nightly snapshot.

Decision: one shared k3s server rather than a managed cluster, because the startup had almost no money and the workloads were small. The trade-off accepted was a single point of failure.

Problem: preview environments would sometimes come up with a broken database, with tables missing. Investigation showed the nightly snapshot job was being killed by the server's out-of-memory killer part way through, leaving a partial dump that restored without errors. The fix was to stream the dump to disk instead of building it in memory, and to check the dump's footer before it was marked good. Lesson: a job that exits is not a job that finished; check the output, not the exit code.

Outcome: 212 pull requests got preview environments over the six months, and the deploy-from-a-laptop practice ended.

Interest in Graphcore: the platform side of the work, especially the scheduling and resource problems, was the most engaging part, and Graphcore's cloud platform is that problem at a much larger scale.
I wrote the GitHub Actions workflow that builds the images and runs the integration tests, and I set up the k3s server.

sources.text:
Project: CI pipeline and preview environments for a student startup's web app (Bristol, part-time, Jan to Jun 2026). The team had five developers and no automated builds; every deploy was done from one laptop.

Goal: every pull request gets a preview environment with its own URL, and merges to main deploy automatically.

Technologies: GitHub Actions, Docker, a small Hetzner server running k3s, Traefik for routing, cert-manager for TLS, and a Postgres database per preview created from a nightly snapshot.

Decision: one shared k3s server rather than a managed cluster, because the startup had almost no money and the workloads were small. The trade-off accepted was a single point of failure.

Problem: preview environments would sometimes come up with a broken database, with tables missing. Investigation showed the nightly snapshot job was being killed by the server's out-of-memory killer part way through, leaving a partial dump that restored without errors. The fix was to stream the dump to disk instead of building it in memory, and to check the dump's footer before it was marked good. Lesson: a job that exits is not a job that finished; check the output, not the exit code.

Outcome: 212 pull requests got preview environments over the six months, and the deploy-from-a-laptop practice ended.

Interest in Graphcore: the platform side of the work, especially the scheduling and resource problems, was the most engaging part, and Graphcore's cloud platform is that problem at a much larger scale.

documents.text:
From January to June 2026 I worked part-time with a five-developer student startup in Bristol to give every pull request its own preview environment and to automate deploys. The team had five developers and no automated builds, and every deploy was done from one laptop. The goal was for every pull request to get a preview environment with its own URL, and for merges to main to deploy automatically. Over the six months, 212 pull requests got preview environments, and the deploy-from-a-laptop practice ended.

The main components were GitHub Actions, Docker, a small Hetzner server running k3s, Traefik for routing, cert-manager for TLS, and a Postgres database per preview created from a nightly snapshot.

One shared k3s server was chosen rather than a managed cluster because the startup had almost no money and the workloads were small. The trade-off accepted was a single point of failure.

Preview environments would sometimes come up with a broken database, with tables missing. Investigation showed the nightly snapshot job was being killed by the server's out-of-memory killer part way through, leaving a partial dump that restored without errors. The fix was to stream the dump to disk instead of building it in memory, and to check the dump's footer before it was marked good. That left the lesson that a job that exits is not a job that finished, and that the output should be checked rather than the exit code.

I wrote the build and push jobs in the GitHub Actions workflow, and Lena wrote the integration-test job. I set up the k3s server.

Dear Graphcore hiring team,

I am applying for the Graduate Cloud Platform Engineer 2027 role at Graphcore.

The platform side of the work, especially the scheduling and resource problems, was the most engaging part, and Graphcore's cloud platform is that problem at a much larger scale.

The project involved a CI pipeline and preview environments for a student startup's web app in Bristol, part-time, from January to June 2026. The team had five developers and no automated builds, and every deploy was done from one laptop. The goal was for every pull request to get a preview environment with its own URL, and for merges to main to deploy automatically. I wrote the build and push jobs in the GitHub Actions workflow, and Lena wrote the integration-test job. I set up the k3s server. Technologies included GitHub Actions, Docker, a small Hetzner server running k3s, Traefik for routing, cert-manager for TLS, and a Postgres database per preview created from a nightly snapshot. One shared k3s server was chosen rather than a managed cluster because the startup had almost no money and the workloads were small.

Preview environments would sometimes come up with a broken database, with tables missing. Investigation showed the nightly snapshot job was being killed by the server's out-of-memory killer part way through, leaving a partial dump that restored without errors. The fix was to stream the dump to disk instead of building it in memory, and to check the dump's footer before it was marked good. 212 pull requests got preview environments over the six months, and the deploy-from-a-laptop practice ended.

Thank you for considering my application.

Kind regards, Ellie
